classification.difficultyReason: The student reads two unlabelled column heights (3 and 6) and applies a single 'twice' clue to assign sushi and tacos. Pizza and burgers are already labelled. There is one relationship to apply and no elimination chain. This is more than simple reading (p11-q3), but far below the four-clue matching in p14-q11.

content.prompt:
Use this clue to work out the missing labels on the $x$ axis of this column chart.

- The number of students who chose tacos is twice the number who chose sushi.

answer.short: Left to right: Pizza, Sushi, Burgers, Tacos.
answer.worked:
The two blank columns have heights $3$ and $6$.
$$6=2\times3$$
Tacos is twice sushi, so tacos is $6$ and sushi is $3$.

Left to right: Pizza, Sushi, Burgers, Tacos.
